coverage_summary: Evaluates zero admissible candidates in Case 1 due to multi-rule admission and feasibility exclusions.
Evaluates exactly one admissible candidate in Cases 2, 4, and 8, filtering out attractive candidates with disqualifying lifecycle, admission, or boundary violations.
Evaluates multiple admissible candidates with interacting trade-offs in Cases 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, and 12.

Verifies inclusive numeric boundaries for latency (latency == latency_budget), age (age == max_age), and cost (cost == max_cost) alongside the exclusive drift boundary (drift == 0.95 fails F6) in Case 4.
Verifies exact ranking ties and deterministic alphanumeric resource identifier tie-breaking in Case 5 and Case 11.

Covers missing optional versus required information including null cost when max_cost is null (Case 6), null age rejection under F7 (Case 6), and null drift rejection under required telemetry (Case 7).

Exhaustively validates policy divergence across lexicographic, latency_first, and locality_cost_first policies, including a complete 3-way winner split in Case 3 and distinct priority shifts in Cases 9, 11, and 12.
Tests stochasticity tolerance boundary condition (tolerance < 0.25 vs tolerance == 0.25) and reset_free stateful penalty combinations in Cases 10 and 11.
Covers degraded and unknown health states surviving feasibility with respective ranking penalties (1 and 2) while offline health and aborting lifecycle trigger hard feasibility exclusions in Case 9.
Validates isolation of admission stage failures (A1, A2, A3, A4) preventing downstream feasibility evaluation in Cases 1, 2, 7, and 8.
specification_questions: Ambiguity in 'admissible' terminology: The contract distinguishes the 'admission' stage (rules A1-A4) from the 'feasibility' stage (rules F1-F8), but subsequently refers to resources entering ranking as 'admissible resources' ('Rank admissible resources by ascending lexicographic tuples... Each ranking contains every admissible resource exactly once'). This dataset interprets 'admissible_resource_ids' and ranking eligibility as candidates that survived BOTH admission and feasibility, matching the rejection stages schema.

Ambiguity in drift requirement rule overlap: Rule F4 states 'If drift_score is required, drift is not null', while rule F6 states 'A null drift is permitted only when drift_score is not required.' When required_telemetry includes 'drift_score' and drift is null, it is ambiguous whether the engine should report failure of F4 only, or both F4 and F6. In this dataset, Case 7 reports F4 as the primary violation.

Fixed zero component in group S: The definition of group S specifies a constant 0 as its second element ([health_penalty, 0, drift_or_1, age / max_age]). While mathematically well-defined, its architectural rationale (e.g., placeholder for future confidence score or reserved capability flag) is unstated.
